Un capital $C_0$ a una rentabilidad anua: A capital $C_0$ at an annual return $r$ becomes $C_0 (1 + r)^n$ after $n$ years. If $a$ is also contributed at the end of each period, the contributions form an annuity: its future value is $a · s_{N¬i} = a · {(1 + i)^N − 1}/i$, with $N$ periods at the rate $i$ per period.
La inflación $π$ es lo que suben los pre: Inflation $π$ is how much prices rise each year. An amount $X$ from $n$ years from now is equivalent today to $X/(1 + π)^n$: it is what can be bought with it at today's prices. With 2 % inflation, prices double in 35 years (rule of 70: $70/2 = 35$).
La ecuación de Fisher separa lo que crec: The Fisher equation separates how much money grows from how much what can be bought grows: $1 + r_{real} = (1 + r)/(1 + π)$, and approximately $r_{real} ≈ r − π$. If the return does not exceed inflation, you are saving while losing purchasing power.
Para tener dentro de n años una cantidad: To have in n years an amount that is worth the same as €X today, you need to gather €X (1 + π)ⁿ of then. What the initial capital does not achieve must be contributed; raising contributions each year with inflation keeps the effort the same in real terms.
